     9	/-!
    10	# Subcanonicity of the étale site, and the section-free transport `picSharp → picEt`
    11	
    12	This file settles a **route** question about the project's central obligation
    13	`Scheme.fgaPicardRepresentability` (`Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean`), and
    14	it settles it in the direction opposite to what that file's docstring and the
    15	board row `AJC.picrep.etale-rep` currently assert.
    16	
    17	## The claim this file refutes
    18	
    19	Clause (1) of the seam asks for representability of the étale-sheafified
    20	functor `PicScheme.picEt C`, while every milestone of the Milne–Kollár campaign
    21	targets the *unsheafified* `PicScheme.picSharp C`. The seam docstring and the
    22	board row both say the gap between them **cannot be bridged without a
    23	`k`-rational point**, on the grounds that the comparison
    24	`PicScheme.picEtComparison C` is Kleiman §2 Thm 2.5 — an isomorphism only under
    25	a section — and that a section is exactly what the owner decision `I-0491`
    26	forbids the headline to carry.
    27	
    28	That reasoning is wrong, and the error is a direction confusion. Kleiman §2
    29	Thm 2.5 is the statement that a section makes the comparison an isomorphism
    30	*with no hypothesis on the presheaf*. But there is a second, entirely
    31	independent, route to the same conclusion: the comparison is the sheafification
    32	unit, and a unit is an isomorphism **exactly when its source is already a
    33	sheaf** (`CategoryTheory.isIso_toSheafify`). A representable functor is a sheaf
    34	for any subcanonical topology. So *if* the campaign delivers representability of
    35	`picSharp`, the source is a sheaf for that reason alone, the unit is an
    36	isomorphism, and no section is involved anywhere.
    37	
    38	The consequence for the route, stated precisely because the board row is
    39	currently priced on its negation: the campaign's endpoint **is** transportable
    40	to clause (1). `picSharp_representableBy_picEt_transport` below is that
    41	transport, proved with no rational-point hypothesis of any kind.
    42	
    43	## What is actually still open
    44	
    45	This file does **not** close the seam. It removes an alleged obstruction, which
    46	is a different thing, and the honest statement of what remains is:
    47	
    48	* the antecedent of every theorem here is representability of `picSharp C`
    49	  over an arbitrary field — campaign milestones J1–J5, G3, G4, B1/B4/B6,
    50	  D2′–D4′, P5 — and **not one of those is discharged**. No theorem in this file
    51	  is applied to a curve anywhere in the project, and none should be reported as
    52	  progress on the existence question;
    53	* what changes is the *shape* of the remaining work. Before this file, a reader
    54	  of the seam docstring concluded that finishing the campaign leaves a further
    55	  unpriced obligation ("represent `picEt` directly, or restate the headline").
    56	  After it, no supplementary étale-representability theorem is needed: `picEt`
    57	  representability follows from `picSharp` representability by `Subcanonical` +
    58	  `isIso_toSheafify`, both already in Mathlib.
    59	
    60	**But the antecedent must not be read as reachable over `k`, and §4 is why.**
    61	The same subcanonicity that powers the transport also proves that a
    62	representable `picSharp` is a *Zariski* sheaf
    63	(`PicScheme.picSharp_isSheaf_zariski_of_representableBy`). Kleiman §2
    64	(L1292–L1302) exhibits a curve over a field for which `picSharp` is **not** a
    65	Zariski sheaf. Contrapositive: representability of `picSharp C` over an
    66	arbitrary field is **false in general**, not merely unproved. So the campaign
    67	milestones that conclude representability of `picSharp`/`picSharpDeg` over `k`
    68	itself — G3 (Galois descent of `picSharp` points) and G4 (the coproduct
    69	assembly) — aim at a statement that cannot be proved as written.
    70	
    71	This is not an argument against the Milne–Kollár route. Everything through J5
    72	runs over a separably closed `k'`, where a section is available and the
    73	obstruction is absent; the break is precisely at the descent step where the
    74	conclusion returns to `k`. The repair the results here name is that the object
    75	descended to `k` must be `picEt`, which *has* the sheaf property that carries
    76	descent, and not `picSharp`, which lacks it. Over `k'` the two agree, by
    77	`isIso_picEtComparison_of_isSheaf` applied to the representability available
    78	there — so J5's output is already a `picEt`-representing scheme after base
    79	change.
    80	
    81	What is **not** established here: that Kleiman's non-sheaf example satisfies
    82	this project's binders (smooth, proper, geometrically integral) — it is quoted
    83	from the reference, not formalised — and no restated G3. The Lean content of §4
    84	is exactly the implication "representable ⇒ Zariski sheaf"; the falsity of the
    85	antecedent is a consequence *given* the quoted counterexample.
    86	
    87	There is one genuine subtlety, and it is not a section. The transport proves
    88	that the *same* scheme represents both functors, so it does not produce
    89	`picSharp` representability out of nothing — it consumes it. Read
    90	`Scheme.picSharp_representableBy_picEt_transport` as: the campaign does not
    91	need a supplementary étale-representability theorem, only the subcanonicity
    92	lemma proved here.
    93	
    94	## Main results
    95	
    96	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.subcanonical_etaleTopology` — the big étale
    97	  topology on schemes is subcanonical. Absent from Mathlib `v4.31` as an
    98	  instance; obtained from `proetaleTopology` (which has one) along
    99	  `Scheme.etaleTopology_le_proetaleTopology` by
   100	  `GrothendieckTopology.Subcanonical.of_le`.
   101	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.subcanonical_etaleTopologyOver` — its localisation
   102	  to `(Sch/k)`, the site the relative Picard presheaf actually lives on.
   103	* `Scheme.PicScheme.isIso_picEtComparison_of_isSheaf` — the section-free
   104	  criterion: if `PicSharp.relPresheaf C` is an étale sheaf then
   105	  `picEtComparison C` is an isomorphism.
   106	* `Scheme.PicScheme.relPresheaf_isSheaf_of_representableBy` — representability
   107	  of `picSharp C` makes `relPresheaf C` an étale sheaf (subcanonicity, then
   108	  reflection along the forgetful functor).
   109	* `Scheme.picSharp_representableBy_picEt_transport` — the transport: a scheme
   110	  representing `picSharp C` also represents `picEt C`, with **no**
   111	  `[HasRationalPoint C]`.
   112	* `Scheme.hasPicSchemeEt_of_picSharp_representability` — the same statement in
   113	  the seam's own packaging: clause (1) of `fgaPicardRepresentability` follows
   114	  from its `picSharp` analogue.
   115	* `Scheme.isIso_picEtComparison_of_picSharp_representability` — and clause (2)
   116	  follows too, *unconditionally*, which is strictly stronger than the seam's
   117	  own `HasRationalPoint C → IsIso …`.
   118	* `Scheme.PicScheme.picSharp_isSheaf_zariski_of_representableBy` — §4: a
   119	  representable `picSharp` is a Zariski sheaf, the implication whose
   120	  contrapositive limits what the campaign's descent step may target.
   121	
   122	## References
   123	
   124	Kleiman, "The Picard scheme" (arXiv:math/0504020), §2 Thm 2.5 (`th:comp`) — the
   125	section route, which this file does not use — and §4 Thm `th:main`.
   126	Board: `AJC.picrep.etale-rep`. Decision: `I-0491`.
   127	-/

   133	open CategoryTheory
   134	
   135	namespace AlgebraicGeometry

   137	namespace Scheme
   138	
   139	/-! ## §1. The étale site is subcanonical -/
   140	
   141	/-- **The big étale topology on schemes is subcanonical**, i.e. every
   142	representable presheaf is an étale sheaf.
   143	
   144	Mathlib `v4.31` supplies this instance for the Zariski, coherent, regular,
   145	extensive and *pro*-étale topologies, but not for the étale one. It costs
   146	nothing: `Scheme.etaleTopology_le_proetaleTopology` and
   147	`GrothendieckTopology.Subcanonical.of_le` (a subtopology of a subcanonical
   148	topology is subcanonical, since the canonical topology is an upper bound).
   149	
   150	This is the lemma that makes the transport of §3 possible, and its absence is
   151	why the seam's route analysis concluded a section was needed. -/
   152	instance subcanonical_etaleTopology : Scheme.etaleTopology.{u}.Subcanonical :=
   153	  GrothendieckTopology.Subcanonical.of_le Scheme.etaleTopology_le_proetaleTopology
   154	
   155	/-- Subcanonicity descends to the localisation `(Sch/k)`, which is the site the
   156	relative Picard presheaf lives on (`Scheme.etaleTopologyOver`,
   157	`Picard/PicEtSheaf.lean`).
   158	
   159	Supplied by `GrothendieckTopology.subcanonical_over` from
   160	`subcanonical_etaleTopology`; recorded as a named theorem because the
   161	`etaleTopologyOver` abbreviation is what every statement downstream mentions. -/
   162	theorem subcanonical_etaleTopologyOver (k : Type u) [Field k] :
   163	    (etaleTopologyOver k).Subcanonical :=
   164	  inferInstance
   165	
   166	namespace PicScheme
   167	
   168	/-! ## §2. The comparison is an isomorphism when the source is a sheaf -/
   169	
   170	/-- **The section-free criterion for the sheafification comparison.**
   171	
   172	`PicScheme.picEtComparison C` is by construction the sheafification unit
   173	`PicSharp.toEtaleSheaf C` whiskered with the forgetful functor. A unit of the
   174	sheafification adjunction is an isomorphism exactly when its source is already
   175	a sheaf (`CategoryTheory.isIso_toSheafify`), so the étale sheaf property of
   176	`PicSharp.relPresheaf C` suffices — and nothing about `C(k)` enters.
   177	
   178	Contrast `picEtComparison_isIso_of_hasRationalPoint`
   179	(`Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean`), which reaches the same conclusion from
   180	Kleiman §2 Thm 2.5 via a section. The two routes are independent; this one is
   181	the one available under the owner decision `I-0491`. -/
   182	theorem isIso_picEtComparison_of_isSheaf {k : Type u} [Field k]
   183	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
   184	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
   185	    (h : Presheaf.IsSheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) (PicSharp.relPresheaf C)) :
   186	    IsIso (picEtComparison C) :=
   187	  haveI : IsIso (PicSharp.toEtaleSheaf C) := isIso_toSheafify _ h
   188	  Functor.isIso_whiskerRight _ _
   189	
   190	/-- **Representability makes the relative Picard presheaf an étale sheaf.**
   191	
   192	Two steps, both structural. A functor represented by a scheme is a sheaf for
   193	the subcanonical étale topology
   194	(`GrothendieckTopology.Subcanonical.isSheaf_of_isRepresentable`, using
   195	`subcanonical_etaleTopologyOver`); and the sheaf property of the
   196	`AddCommGrpCat`-valued `relPresheaf C` is *equivalent* to that of its
   197	underlying type-valued functor `picSharp C = relPresheaf C ⋙ forget _`, because
   198	the forgetful functor of a concrete algebraic category preserves limits and
   199	reflects isomorphisms (`Presheaf.isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_forget`).
   200	
   201	The hypothesis is a `RepresentableBy` for an arbitrary `X`, not for
   202	`PicScheme C`, so this does not silently consume the seam. -/
   203	theorem relPresheaf_isSheaf_of_representableBy {k : Type u} [Field k]
   204	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
   205	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
   206	    {X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))}
   207	    (rep : (picSharp C).RepresentableBy X) :
   208	    Presheaf.IsSheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) (PicSharp.relPresheaf C) := by
   209	  haveI : (picSharp C).IsRepresentable := ⟨X, ⟨rep⟩⟩
   210	  have hsh : Presieve.IsSheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) (picSharp C) :=
   211	    GrothendieckTopology.Subcanonical.isSheaf_of_isRepresentable _
   212	  rw [Presheaf.isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_forget (s := CategoryTheory.forget AddCommGrpCat.{u+1}),
   213	    CategoryTheory.isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_of_type]
   214	  exact hsh
   215	
   216	end PicScheme
   217	
   218	/-! ## §3. The transport, with no rational point anywhere -/
   219	
   220	/-- **The transport: a scheme representing `picSharp C` also represents
   221	`picEt C`, with no hypothesis on `C(k)`.**
   222	
   223	This is the statement the seam docstring and the board row `AJC.picrep.etale-rep`
   224	declare impossible without a section. The proof composes §1 and §2: the
   225	representing scheme makes `relPresheaf C` an étale sheaf
   226	(`relPresheaf_isSheaf_of_representableBy`, i.e. subcanonicity), being a sheaf
   227	makes the sheafification unit an isomorphism
   228	(`isIso_picEtComparison_of_isSheaf`), and `Functor.RepresentableBy.ofIso`
   229	carries the representation across it.
   230	
   231	Note what is and is not proved. `X` is *given* here — the theorem consumes
   232	`picSharp` representability rather than producing it, and that antecedent is
   233	exactly the undischarged output of the Milne–Kollár campaign. What the theorem
   234	establishes is that no *further* representability theorem is needed on top of
   235	the campaign, contradicting the "eleventh item" pricing. -/
   236	noncomputable def picSharp_representableBy_picEt_transport {k : Type u} [Field k]
   237	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
   238	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
   239	    {X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))}
   240	    (rep : (PicScheme.picSharp C).RepresentableBy X) :
   241	    (PicScheme.picEt C).RepresentableBy X :=
   242	  rep.ofIso (@asIso _ _ _ _ (PicScheme.picEtComparison C)
   243	    (PicScheme.isIso_picEtComparison_of_isSheaf C
   244	      (PicScheme.relPresheaf_isSheaf_of_representableBy C rep)))
   245	
   246	/-- **Clause (1) of the seam follows from its `picSharp` analogue.**
   247	
   248	Same content as `picSharp_representableBy_picEt_transport`, packaged in the
   249	seam's own existential shape so the comparison with
   250	`Scheme.fgaPicardRepresentability` is direct: the local-finiteness and
   251	separatedness conjuncts are carried across unchanged, because the transport
   252	does not move the representing scheme — it is the *same* `X`.
   253	
   254	The hypothesis is stated as the `picSharp`-shaped existential rather than as
   255	`[HasPicScheme C]`, deliberately: `HasPicScheme` pins the witness to
   256	`PicScheme C` and has no instance, so quantifying over it would make this
   257	theorem consume an uninhabited class. Here the witness is universally
   258	quantified and the statement is a genuine implication. -/
   259	theorem hasPicSchemeEt_of_picSharp_representability {k : Type u} [Field k]
   260	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
   261	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
   262	    (h : ∃ X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)),
   263	        Nonempty ((PicScheme.picSharp C).RepresentableBy X) ∧
   264	          LocallyOfFiniteType X.hom ∧ IsSeparated X.hom) :
   265	    ∃ X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)),
   266	      Nonempty ((PicScheme.picEt C).RepresentableBy X) ∧
   267	        LocallyOfFiniteType X.hom ∧ IsSeparated X.hom := by
   268	  obtain ⟨X, ⟨rep⟩, hft, hsep⟩ := h
   269	  exact ⟨X, ⟨picSharp_representableBy_picEt_transport C rep⟩, hft, hsep⟩
   270	
   271	/-- **Clause (2) follows too, and unconditionally** — which is strictly stronger
   272	than the seam's own second conjunct `HasRationalPoint C → IsIso …`.
   273	
   274	Given representability of `picSharp C`, the comparison
   275	`PicScheme.picEtComparison C` is an isomorphism outright, with no section. So
   276	under the campaign's endpoint the rational-point hypothesis of Kleiman §2
   277	Thm 2.5 becomes redundant *for this curve*: it was buying a sheaf property that
   278	representability already supplies.
   279	
   280	This is not a proof of Kleiman 2.5 — that theorem asserts the comparison is an
   281	isomorphism from the section alone, with no representability input, and remains
   282	unformalised. -/
   283	theorem isIso_picEtComparison_of_picSharp_representability {k : Type u} [Field k]
   284	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
   285	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
   286	    {X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))}
   287	    (rep : (PicScheme.picSharp C).RepresentableBy X) :
   288	    IsIso (PicScheme.picEtComparison C) :=
   289	  PicScheme.isIso_picEtComparison_of_isSheaf C
   290	    (PicScheme.relPresheaf_isSheaf_of_representableBy C rep)
   291	
   292	/-! ## §4. The limit on the antecedent: representable implies *Zariski* sheaf
   293	
   294	The transport of §3 says the campaign needs no supplementary étale
   295	representability theorem. This section says where the campaign may not put its
   296	conclusion, and the two together are what actually price the board row.
   297	
   298	Attribution: this direction was pointed out by `review-ajc` on the §1–§3
   299	commit, as a corollary of `relPresheaf_isSheaf_of_representableBy`. -/
   300	
   301	namespace PicScheme
   302	
   303	/-- **A representable `picSharp` is a Zariski sheaf.**
   304	
   305	Immediate from subcanonicity of the *Zariski* topology on `(Sch/k)`
   306	(`Scheme.subcanonical_zariskiTopology` through
   307	`GrothendieckTopology.subcanonical_over`) — the étale route of §1 is not even
   308	needed, though `zariskiTopologyOver_le_etaleTopologyOver` (`Picard/PicEtSheaf.lean`)
   309	would also transport it from there.
   310	
   311	**What this rules out.** The seam docstring
   312	(`Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean`, "Why sheafifying is what makes an
   313	unconditional statement possible") argues *in prose* that an unconditional
   314	`RepresentableBy` against `picSharp` is FALSE rather than unproved, because
   315	Kleiman §2 (L1292–L1302) gives a curve whose `picSharp` is not a Zariski sheaf
   316	while a representable functor is a sheaf for any subcanonical topology. This
   317	theorem is the second half of that argument, as a Lean statement rather than as
   318	prose. Its contrapositive therefore says: over an arbitrary field, no scheme
   319	represents `picSharp C` in general.

According to descent theory, every representable functor is a sheaf in
the Zariski topology \emdash in fact, in the \'etale and fppf
topologies as well.  Therefore, the absolute Picard functor $\Pic_X$ is never
representable.  So, in the hope of obtaining a representable functor
that differs as little as possible from $\Pic_X$, we now define a
sequence of three successively more promising relative functors.

\begin{dfn}\label{df:Pfs}
  The {\it relative Picard functor} $\Pic_{X/S}$ is defined by
	$$\Pic_{X/S}(T):=\Pic(X_T)\big/\Pic(T).$$
 Denote its associated sheaves in the Zariski, \'etale, and fppf
topologies  by
	$$\Pic_{(X/S)\zar},\ \Pic_{(X/S)\et},\
	\Pic_{(X/S)\fppf}.$$
 \end{dfn}

We now have a sequence of five Picard functors, and each one maps
naturally into the next.  So each one maps naturally into any of its
successors.  If the latter functor is one of the three just displayed,
then it is a sheaf in the indicated topology; in fact, it is the sheaf
associated to any one of its predecessors, and the map between them is
the natural map from a presheaf to its associated sheaf, as is easy to
check.  In particular, the three displayed sheaves are the sheaves
associated to the absolute Picard functor $\Pic_X$, as well as to the
relative Picard functor $\Pic_{X/S}$.

representable so often in practice.

$\mc L'$ to $X_{T''}$ are isomorphic \emdash or to put it informally, the

Take an indeterminate $z$, and identify $\bb C$ with $\bb

invertible sheaf $\mc L$ on $\I P^1_k$ is determined, up to isomorphism,

\cite[Cor.~6.17, p.~145]{Ha83}.  Hence, the two pullbacks of $\vf^*\mc
O(1)$ to $X_{\bb C\ox_\bb R\bb C}$ are isomorphic.  Thus
